Stages, in the order each pass runs them:
  STAGE            CONTACT      KEY     WHAT IT DOES
  crtsh            third party          Subdomains from certificate transparency logs (crt.sh)
  shodan           third party  shodan  Addresses, hostnames and ports Shodan reports in each in-scope netblock
  providerranges*  third party          Address ranges cloud and CDN providers publish, to tell shared infrastructure
  resolve*         third party          A and AAAA records of each hostname and root, from public resolvers
  wildcard*        third party          Lookups of random labels in each zone, to detect wildcard DNS
  httpprobe        target               HTTP and HTTPS services on each hostname and open port, as a browser sees them
  ports            target               TCP handshakes to the configured ports, keeping any banner sent unprompted

Third-party stages ask public sources and resolvers, and run under --passive. Target stages
contact the target's own systems: they are skipped under --passive, and unless --authorised
has confirmed, on this run or an earlier one, that you are authorised. A stage with a KEY needs keys.<KEY> and is not-configured without it; a key in
brackets is optional. --redo <stage> performs every check of one stage again, and --skip <stage>
turns one off, except the stages marked *, which other stages' safety depends on.
